Tap here, then use the VoiceType keyboard or the bubble…

The floating bubble needs Android's Accessibility permission to type into other apps. Here is exactly what VoiceType does with it:

What it does
• Finds the text field that currently has focus, and inserts the text you just dictated at your cursor (keeping what was already there).
• Notices when the on-screen keyboard opens or closes, so the bubble can hide.

What it does not do
• It does not read, log or store anything else on your screen.
• It cannot send anything anywhere: VoiceType has no internet permission at all. You can verify this in Settings → Apps → VoiceType → Permissions, and the app works in airplane mode.

How to turn it on
Tap the button below, choose "Installed apps" (or "Downloaded apps"), tap "VoiceType bubble typing" and switch it on.

If the switch is greyed out (Android 13+ "restricted setting" for apps not installed from a store): open Settings → Apps → VoiceType, tap ⋮ in the top-right corner → "Allow restricted settings", then come back and try again.

You don't need this if you only use the VoiceType keyboard.
